Maintenance Report — MNT-0027-004

Asset: WELL-0027 (SW-23 Well 027, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 08 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 02 Aug 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 603 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0027-0036 on 2023-07-06 Report written: 04 Aug 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0027-0036 showed the wellhead at 38.7 °C with the air at 35.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 23 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0027-013

Asset: WELL-0027 (SW-23 Well 027, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 13 Jul 2024 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jul 2024 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 411 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0027-0089 on 2024-07-11 Report written: 01 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0027-0089 showed the wellhead at 36.7 °C with the air at 34.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit

Maintenance Report — MNT-0027-014

Asset: WELL-0027 (SW-23 Well 027, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Sep 2024 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 79 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0027-0097 on 2024-09-05 Report written: 11 Sep 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0027-0097 showed the wellhead at 32.9 °C with the air at 29.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0027-016

Asset: WELL-0027 (SW-23 Well 027, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 20 Dec 2024 08:00 · Finished: 20 Dec 2024 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 12 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0027-0112 on 2024-12-19 Report written: 21 Dec 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0027-0112 at 15:30 on 2024-12-19 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.7% of the pad area, estimated 1.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 6.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 262 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 210 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0027-016 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.72% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0027-021

Asset: WELL-0027 (SW-23 Well 027, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Jun 2025 08:00 · Finished: 17 Jun 2025 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 247 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0027-0136 on 2025-06-05 Report written: 18 Jun 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0027-0136 showed the wellhead at 33.6 °C with the air at 31.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0027-021 (WS-06).
